findings.title: Signal-to-power class is grouped by power net, not by voltage, so a high-voltage gap can still shrink to a low-voltage gap
findings.detail: The diff's stated reason for the new class is that a signal-to-power gap 'sees up to the DC-link voltage, unlike a gate-to-Kelvin gap'. That is false for 4 of the 12 pairs the class contains. layout.py:80 says the HS Kelvin source is at PHASE potential and the LS Kelvin source at DC- potential. So GATE_HS/KELVIN_HS to PHASE and GATE_LS/KELVIN_LS to DC- see only the gate-drive voltage (about 20 V), while GATE_HS to DC- or GATE_LS to PHASE see the full DC link. measure_rules takes the minimum over each spacing_signal_{dcp,phase,dcm} class. A reference that runs a signal trace next to its own source copper (common practice for gate-loop inductance) therefore sets a small class value, and a derivative can then move a high-voltage pair down to it. This is the same failure the change sets out to fix (a high-voltage gap inheriting a low-voltage gap's value), only moved inside the new class. A DRC that is meant to guard isolation accepts a 3x cut in a high-voltage clearance on a reference that is DRC-clean under the defaults.
findings.evidence: Scratch script using the test fixture. The reference replaces GATE_LS with union(box(36,5.5,38.5,17.5), box(35,17.5,38.5,26)) mm, so GATE_LS (referenced to DC-) sits 1.0 mm from DC-. check(ref)==[]; measure_rules gives gap_signal_dcm=1.0e-3 and check(ref, rules)==[]. The derivative moves GATE_HS to box(3,17.5,19,19.5), cutting the GATE_HS-to-DC- gap (PHASE potential against DC-, full DC link) from 3.0 mm to 1.0 mm. check(der, rules) returns [], no violation.
findings.suggested_check: Group spacing by potential: signal net of switch S against power net P is low-voltage only if P is S's source net (HS->PHASE, LS->DC-), otherwise high-voltage. Add a test that the counterexample above produces a min_spacing violation.

findings.title: The leftover 'signal-signal' class also mixes HS and LS signals; the new test uses a high-voltage pair as its low-voltage example
findings.detail: The diff's comments and tests treat the remaining spacing_other pairs as low-voltage ('signal-signal only', 'unlike a gate-to-Kelvin gap'). But any HS signal net (PHASE potential) against any LS signal net (DC- potential) sees the full DC link. The new test test_hv_signal_to_power_gap_cannot_shrink_to_a_signal_gap builds its 'tight signal gap' reference from KELVIN_HS to KELVIN_LS at 1.0 mm, which is itself a high-voltage pair. Conversely, a reference with a tight same-switch gate-Kelvin pair (low voltage) lets an HS-to-LS signal gap shrink to that value. This was already possible before the change, but the change's documentation now states the opposite.
findings.evidence: The reference replaces KELVIN_LS with union(box(20,1.5,38.5,3.5), box(36,1.5,38.5,4.5)) mm, so KELVIN_LS sits 1.0 mm from GATE_LS (both referenced to DC-). check(ref)==[]; gap_other_min=1.0e-3; ref is clean under its own rules. The derivative KELVIN_HS=box(3,1.5,19,3.5) cuts the KELVIN_HS-to-KELVIN_LS gap (PHASE vs DC-) from 3.0 to 1.0 mm. check(der, rules)==[].
findings.suggested_check: Include HS-signal vs LS-signal pairs in the high-voltage group, and correct the test comment that calls KELVIN_HS/KELVIN_LS a signal-only (low-voltage) gap.

findings.title: Setting the new max_signal_wire_length loosens a stricter per-pad limit
findings.detail: signal_length_range uses max_signal_wire_length when it is set and ignores max_gate_wire_length / max_kelvin_wire_length. Adding the general limit can therefore silently relax an existing per-pad limit. The upper bound should be the smaller of the two. measure_rules never sets this field, so the measured-rules flow is not affected.
findings.evidence: Fixture gate wire of 9.271 mm. DesignRules(max_gate_wire_length=8.771 mm) gives 1 signal_wire_length violation. Adding max_signal_wire_length=20 mm gives 0 violations.
findings.suggested_check: Set hi = min(max_signal_wire_length, per-pad limit) when both are given, and add a test for it.

findings.title: measure_rules docstring says it measures max_signal_wire_length; it does not
findings.detail: The docstring says min/max_signal_wire_length are 'the reference's own smallest and largest values', but the code sets only min_signal_wire_length and leaves max_signal_wire_length as None. The upper bound actually comes from max_gate/kelvin_wire_length, which is functionally fine.
findings.evidence: measure_rules(fixture()) gives rules.max_signal_wire_length=None, while max_gate_wire_length=9.270592e-3 and max_kelvin_wire_length=7.687264e-3.

findings.title: New default behaviour: signal wires thicker than max_wire_diameter (0.5 mm) are now rejected under DEFAULT_RULES
findings.detail: signal_diameter_range uses max_wire_diameter as its default upper bound, so DEFAULT_RULES add a signal_wire_diameter check that did not exist before. This is reasonable and the full unit suite passes, but it is a change to default behaviour for the signal-wire checks, whereas the spacing fields are documented as 'unchanged when unset'.
findings.evidence: test_signal_wire_diameter_range asserts that 0.6 mm is rejected under DEFAULT_RULES.
